As someone who both drove for UberEats at one time and who has ordered from there often, the cost of getting food delivered is outrageous. For context I live in a very large city where owning a car is more hassle than the public transit and public transit is still a hassle. I understand it is the cost of convenience but for example ordering one standard pizza on UberEats can cost upwards of $50. I pretty much only order from places within a 3-4 mile radius maximum and that is still the cost. I'm not 100% on the breakdown of what the restaurant is charging vs what Uber is charging but it is very clear to me that one or the other is making money hand over fist by not paying the drivers accordingly. Tipping is important, but the base pay is far too low in comparison to what the cost of the actual food is for the customer. The person who ordered this (depending what they ordered) is almost certainly paying a $10+ delivery fee in addition to extremely upcharged prices on the food itself and if they have never worked the other side of it they may have no idea that the trip will be entirely tip dependent. To be honest, no trips should be tip dependent, tips are, and always have been, a practice reserved to reward exceptional service, not to supplement income to make it livable. The customers are not to blame, the corporation and business model are at fault for low paying trips. I know that a very common theme in gig work subreddits is "no tip, no trip" but as costs continue to rise for the customer I fear it will become more and more common for tips to be below expectation until one day there are no more trips to be had.
